text: ADDITION (round-35b, user, verbatim intent): DELETE the tiny green activity dots on panes entirely — the quiet 5px TabActivityIndicator dots (src/components/Sidebar/TabActivityIndicator.tsx, ct-tab-activity-quiet, orchestrator-accent + presence-color variants) that signal 'this pane took a task/plan'. User verdict: meaningless noise, looks broken. Remove the component usage from tab rows (and the component + its test if nothing else consumes it — grep first); the task/plan attribution story is already carried by the composer strips (Orchestrating/Planning/Working on), the group containment, and the task line under working rows. No replacement indicator. Criterion addition: zero activity dots render on any tab row (component assertion + grep proves TabActivityIndicator unused or deleted).

REFINEMENT ROUND (round-38, user: 'better, now make it elegant'). Four precise moves, keep everything else: (1) HEADERS EARN THEIR ROW — the MANAGERS header is a full shouting row for a section that almost always holds exactly one planner whose badge already says PLANNER. Rule: render a section micro-header ONLY when the group has both sections populated OR a section has >1 member; a group with just one planner shows no MANAGERS header at all (planner-first ordering + badge carry the meaning). When shown: 8px, tracking-wide, muted 40%, no extra top gap. (2) BADGES LOSE THE BOX — bordered pills x2 per row is chrome noise. Role becomes borderless small-caps colored text (accent hue for ORCHESTRATOR, planner hue for PLANNER), model stays a muted lowercase suffix after the middot: 'Brahms  ORCHESTRATOR · opus' — one quiet line, zero boxes. Keep the pill ONLY if a hover/focus state needs a hit target (it does not — badges are not buttons). (3) LINE GOES HAIRLINE — containment line 1px (not 2-3px block), full group-body height INCLUDING any header row, presence color ~30% alpha, inset 10px; on group-head hover the line brightens slightly (+15%) — belonging becomes a felt affordance, not a diagram. Current state shows uneven partial segments with inconsistent hues between groups — the line must be one continuous element per group, same alpha rule for all. (4) RHYTHM — inner gaps 4px between child rows, 6px before a section header, 10px between groups; chevron ghosts in on row hover only. Acceptance: updated screenshot vs this spec; the single-planner group renders exactly three visual elements (head row, line, planner row) and nothing else.

Accepted and merged in 42598f58, carried by current head 5e679362. Group containment matches refined spec: one visual block per orchestration, conditional headers, borderless role/model text, 1px hairline containment, collapse counts, planner generated names hardened against literal Planner, TabActivityIndicator deleted. Gates passed: TS focused tests, tsc, orchestration_pair 11/11, build.sh check, pre-push cargo check/fmt/clippy. Dali cleaned eight lane/dev/worktree.

SCOPE REFINEMENT (round-43, user, verbatim intent): the orchestration group must collapse LIKE A WORKSPACE — a neat, pleasant handle on the RIGHT side of the group head row, mirroring the workspace collapse affordance; default state EXPANDED. Current code already has the mechanism (SidebarWorkspaceTabs.tsx collapsedGroups state, TabItem.tsx group-collapse-toggle, collapsedSummary '1 manager · 2 workers') but renders a 12px chevron on the LEFT before the provider glyph — wrong side, wrong feel. Required: (1) move the toggle to the RIGHT edge of the orchestrator head row, visually matching the workspace handle (same size/color/rotation animation family as WorkspaceItem.tsx chevron: muted, hover brightens, 320ms cubic-bezier rotate); (2) default expanded stays (new Set() — already correct); (3) collapsed head keeps the summary line; the containment hairline and children disappear as one unit; (4) keep data-testid group-collapse-toggle so existing GroupContainment tests survive — extend them with a right-side position assertion (toggle is the LAST interactive element in the head row) and a default-expanded assertion. This folds into the same elegance pass — one lane, not a second task.
